closes: C4. STATUS carries no $filter today and never queries by reference or email; it reads an unfiltered top-N of Global Tracking Queue.

remove.why: Boundary. An anonymous endpoint must not read the internal task register.
STATUS is a read. These are inherited from the submission flow it was copied from.

actions.name: Get_Rate_Limit_Status_Source
actions.why: Stops a scraper walking the reference space.

actions.name: Update_Rate_Limit_Status_Source
actions.why: Run only when the bucket exists and its window is current.

actions.name: Create_Rate_Limit_Status_Source
actions.why: Run only when the bucket is absent or its window has rolled over.

actions.name: Get_Rate_Limit_Status_Reference
actions.why: A reference is guessable by construction - NITDA-<year>-<n>. This bucket stops someone hammering one they have guessed.

actions.name: Update_Rate_Limit_Status_Reference
actions.why: Run only when the bucket exists and its window is current.

actions.name: Create_Rate_Limit_Status_Reference
actions.why: Run only when the bucket is absent or its window has rolled over.

actions.name: Get_Submission_By_Reference
actions.why: Filters ReferenceId, which is indexed and enforceUnique, rather than Title, which is neither. The email prefers the PROOF ROW and falls back to the body only on the unproofed path - Directive E: once a caller presents a proof, the flow must not authenticate with the field the proof replaces. A miss and a mismatch answer the same 404 so the endpoint is not an oracle for which references exist.

actions.name: Consume_Verification_Proof
actions.why: Directive A. Runs AFTER the registry lookup, never before it: consuming first burns a valid single-use proof on a mistyped reference and forces a fresh email round trip to fix a client-side mistake. Ships as the If-Match conditional write specified in 06-writeback-citizen-actions.json.

actions.name: Create_Flow_Telemetry
actions.why: HOUSE STANDARD. Place inside Scope_Flow_Data_Capture, beside the existing Compose_Flow_Run_Record - not on the request path. The values are the standard variable set the skeleton already initialises; if this flow has no Scope_Flow_Data_Capture, add the scope first, because that is the conformance gap rather than this action.

responseProjection.why: The STATUS allow-list in PORTAL_DATA_CONTRACT.md, which is closed: a field absent from it is not thereby permitted. Names on the left are the JSON keys track.js reads; the column each is read from is in brackets.

removed.attachmentCount: Projected before, and not permitted: attachments are on the contract never-list and the allow-list is closed. track.js never read it.

added.category: track.js renders it as Registry category.
added.subject: track.js renders it as the record heading.
added.timeline[].note: track.js renders it under each timeline entry.

verification: npm run wiring   # STATUS moves from 0/7 to 7/7 and its two crossings clear
Submit, then read the status back with the reference and email - the timeline must show the received event

buildStandard.placement: Work in Scope_<Purpose> under Scope_Global; failure path in the catch scope; answer through Compose__Standard_Response_Revised then Response; run record in Scope_Flow_Data_Capture.

standardConformance.decision: D7 - the standard work rides along with each visit rather than waiting for a sixth pass. The flow is already open, and adding a catch scope to a flow whose actions you have just rewritten costs a fraction of coming back to it.
standardConformance.order: Do the standard work FIRST, before the SharePoint actions in Step B. The variables and Scope_Global have to exist before an action can reference them, and moving actions into a scope afterwards is where things get dropped.

missing.title: Wrap the work in Scope_Global

missing.title: Add Scope_Flow_Data_Capture
missing.how: Add a Scope named Scope_Flow_Data_Capture as a top-level peer of Scope_Global, with 'Configure run after' set to Succeeded, Failed, Skipped and Timed out - it must run whatever happened.
missing.why: The observability harness twenty-three flows already carry. Adding it is what makes this flow visible in the same way as the rest of the estate.

missing.title: Compose the versioned run record
missing.how: Inside Scope_Flow_Data_Capture, add a Compose named Compose_Flow_Run_Record.
missing.copyFrom: Any conforming flow - Fetch_Tasks_POST is the cleanest. Copy Compose_Flow_Run_Record verbatim; it reads only workflow(), trigger(), the redaction composes and the standard variables, so it is portable between flows unchanged.
missing.why: capture_version 2.0.0, with its draft-07 schema alongside. Copying rather than rewriting is the point - a second dialect of the record is worse than none.

missing.title: Redact headers before capture
missing.how: Inside Scope_Flow_Data_Capture, add a Compose named Compose_Redacted_Headers, running after Compose_Redacted_Queries.
missing.why: Without it the observability harness becomes the leak.

wireInto.note: Same: an unconsumed Compose redacts nothing. Compose_Flow_Run_Record must also be moved to run after Compose_Redacted_Headers, or it composes before the value exists.

missing.title: Redact the query string before capture
missing.how: Inside Scope_Flow_Data_Capture, add a Compose named Compose_Redacted_Queries. Place it first in that scope, immediately after Get_Flow_Definition.
missing.why: sig is the trigger credential and code is the one-time password. On the verification flows this is the difference between telemetry and a log of every OTP issued.

wireInto.note: Adding the Compose without this leaves it inert: the run record captures no query string at all, and the conformance check still passes. The rule is about what reaches telemetry, not about an action existing.
